title: Representative Ranking for Deliberation in the Public Sphere
findings: This paper does not present any findings related to religion. Its primary finding is that enforcing a 'justified representation' (JR) constraint in comment ranking can increase the inclusion of diverse viewpoints with a low 'price' (i.e., minimal negative impact) on other objectives like user engagement or conversational quality, especially when user opinions are clustered.

measurement_description: The paper does not benchmark or measure anything specifically related to faith or religion. The term 'religion' is used as an example of a demographic category that traditional algorithmic fairness methods rely on, which the paper's proposed method (Justified Representation) is designed to avoid. A hypothetical example of an intersectional group mentions 'Jewish white males', but this is not part of any measurement.
